concepts.name: 3.13 batched(strict=True)
concepts.description: Python 3.13 added strict= to itertools.batched; strict=True raises ValueError when the final batch is shorter than n.

concepts.name: 3.13 copy.replace
concepts.description: Python 3.13 added copy.replace(obj, **changes), a common replacement protocol supported by dataclasses, named tuples, datetime types, and custom __replace__ implementations.

concepts.name: 3.13 Queue.shutdown
concepts.description: Python 3.13 added Queue.shutdown() and the ShutDown exception for explicit producer-consumer queue termination.

concepts.name: 3.13 typing.TypeIs
concepts.description: Python 3.13 added typing.TypeIs for user-defined type-narrowing predicates whose true and false branches can both narrow more intuitively than TypeGuard.

questions.prompt: Require every insertion batch to contain exactly 100 records.

content.template:
# batched() groups an iterable into fixed-size chunks.
from itertools import batched
for batch in batched(records, 100, {{answer}}):
    insert(batch)

questions.explanation: Python 3.13 added strict= to itertools.batched; strict=True raises ValueError when the final batch is shorter than n. for batch in batched(records, 100, strict=True): ... enforces exact batch size. The validation happens as the iterator is consumed, because batched is lazy.

questions.prompt: Create a modified copy without mutating config.
questions.explanation: Python 3.13 added copy.replace(obj, **changes), a common replacement protocol supported by dataclasses, named tuples, datetime types, and custom __replace__ implementations. new_config = copy.replace(config, retries=5) creates a modified copy without mutating the original. copy.replace is not a general deep copy; it constructs a replacement with selected fields changed.

{{answer}}

questions.explanation: Python 3.13 added Queue.shutdown() and the ShutDown exception for explicit producer-consumer queue termination. q.shutdown() prevents future growth while allowing already queued work to wind down normally by default. shutdown(immediate=True) breaks the usual join invariant by draining work immediately, so it should be used deliberately.

questions.prompt: Annotate this predicate for Python 3.13 type narrowing.
questions.explanation: Python 3.13 added typing.TypeIs for user-defined type-narrowing predicates whose true and false branches can both narrow more intuitively than TypeGuard. def is_str(value: object) -> TypeIs[str]: return isinstance(value, str) communicates narrowing to a type checker. TypeIs is a typing contract: the function's runtime boolean logic must actually satisfy the type relationship it claims.
